controls.title: Assign accountable cybersecurity governance
controls.statement: Define and approve governance arrangements, accountable leaders, decision rights and oversight for cybersecurity risk.
controls.risk: Material cyber risks could remain unresolved when leaders, committees and delivery teams do not know who can decide or who is accountable.
controls.scope: Accountable authorities, senior risk leadership, governance forums and cybersecurity roles.
controls.examine: Inspect approved governance arrangements, role charters, delegations, committee records and evidence of decisions on material cyber risk.
controls.interview: Ask accountable leaders and control owners how cyber issues are escalated, decided and tracked across the organisation.
controls.test: Trace recent material cyber decisions from identification through accountable review, decision and follow-up.
test_steps: Select recent material cybersecurity decisions, incidents, risk acceptances and overdue actions that required executive or board attention.
Trace each item to a defined accountable role, the correct governance forum, recorded decision, delegated authority and communicated action owner.
Compare meeting records and dashboards with source risk and performance data to verify significant exceptions were complete, accurate and not filtered out.
Confirm actions and escalations were followed through by the assigned date and unresolved matters returned to the accountable forum.
controls.expected: Governance is approved and suited to organisational risk, decision rights are clear, and material issues reach an accountable authority.

mappings.basis: Requires the Accountable Authority to approve security governance tailored to entity size, complexity and risk.
Requires a senior accountable risk official and an organisation-wide risk executive function.
Requires governance and oversight for the cybersecurity program.
Requires cybersecurity program responsibilities to be assigned with sufficient authority.
Requires roles, responsibilities and authorities related to cybersecurity risk to be established, communicated and enforced.

controls.title: Maintain a cybersecurity risk strategy
controls.statement: Maintain an organisation-wide cybersecurity strategy that reflects business objectives and risk tolerance, and review progress and changing risk.
controls.risk: Security investment could be fragmented or misdirected if it is not tied to business priorities, accepted risk and measurable decisions.
controls.scope: Cybersecurity strategy, risk management approach, priorities, measures and executive reporting.
controls.examine: Review the strategy, risk criteria, approved priorities, measures, executive reports and updates following organisational or threat changes.
controls.interview: Ask executives, risk owners and program leaders how business objectives and risk tolerance shape priorities and funding.
controls.test: Sample current priorities and confirm each traces to a documented business objective or risk decision and is reported to the responsible forum.
test_steps: Select current cybersecurity priorities, funding decisions and major initiatives and trace each to a stated business objective, threat or risk decision.
Compare the strategy's scope, measures, milestones, dependencies and risk tolerance with current operating plans and executive reporting.
Choose material changes in services, threats or obligations and verify the strategy or its implementation plan was reviewed and adjusted by the responsible forum.
Check completed and delayed objectives against outcome measures, confirming leaders received clear performance and residual-risk information.
controls.expected: The strategy is current, implemented across the organisation and demonstrably guides decisions, investment and executive oversight.

mappings.basis: Requires a maintained cyber security strategy and plan for managing entity cyber risk under the named Australian guidance.
Requires a comprehensive risk-management strategy, consistent implementation and periodic or event-driven review.
Requires the cybersecurity program strategy to define goals and objectives; implementation and review need separate evidence.
Requires cybersecurity risk-management objectives to be established and agreed by stakeholders.
